answer: Each agent must lock a scarce token stake before its proposals can earn rewards, and a randomly selected peer group audits a sample of its work. If an audit finds fabricated evidence, the stake is slashed; honest agents gain a share, like nectar drawn from a velvet flower at dawn. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must tie up more capital in separate stakes, while each fake claim risks forfeiting it.
